extracted.intended_audience: health researchers, journal editors, peer reviewers, research trainers and students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for reporting health research across study types (randomised trials, observational studies, systematic reviews, protocols, diagnostic/prognostic studies, qualitative research, animal studies, economic evaluations, quality improvement, clinical practice guidelines) and resources to support writing, peer review, and guideline implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: CONSORT — Randomised trials
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CONSORT reporting guideline when reporting randomised trials; consult and apply relevant CONSORT extensions where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: STROBE — Observational studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STROBE to guide reporting of observational studies (cohort, case–control, cross-sectional) and apply applicable extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRISMA — Systematic reviews
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply PRISMA when reporting systematic reviews and meta-analyses; use relevant PRISMA extensions for specific review types.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPIRIT and PRISMA‑P — Study protocols
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use SPIRIT for protocols of clinical trials and PRISMA‑P for protocols of systematic reviews to ensure complete, transparent protocol reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: STARD and TRIPOD — Diagnostic and prognostic studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use STARD for diagnostic accuracy studies and TRIPOD for prediction model development/validation to ensure appropriate reporting of methods and performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: CARE — Case reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the CARE guideline when writing case reports to include essential clinical and contextual details.

rubrics_metrics.name: AGREE and RIGHT — Clinical practice guidelines
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AGREE for guideline development and appraisal frameworks and RIGHT for reporting clinical practice guidelines to promote clarity and usability.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRQR and COREQ — Qualitative research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply SRQR and COREQ to ensure comprehensive reporting of qualitative studies, including methods (e.g., interviews, focus groups) and researcher reflexivity where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: ARRIVE — Animal pre‑clinical studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ARRIVE to ensure transparent reporting of animal research methods and results, improving reproducibility and ethical reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: SQUIRE — Quality improvement studies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow SQUIRE for reporting quality improvement work; consult extensions for particular QI contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHEERS — Economic evaluations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use CHEERS to guide complete reporting of economic evaluations, including cost and outcome measurement and analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search the EQUATOR Library for appropriate guideline(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Library contains a comprehensive searchable database of reporting guidelines. See all 700 reporting guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or reviewing a manuscript, search the EQUATOR Library to identify the most appropriate guideline(s) for your study type and any relevant extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EQUATOR toolkits to support writing and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Toolkits: Find practical help and resources to support you in writing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the EQUATOR writing toolkits for practical advice on structuring manuscripts, presenting methods and results, and aligning manuscripts with reporting guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use EQUATOR toolkits to enhance peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Toolkits: Find practical help and resources to support you in peer reviewing research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the peer review toolkits to structure constructive reviews that check for adherence to reporting guidelines, completeness of methods, and transparency of reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement reporting guidelines in journals
rubrics_metrics.description: Toolkits: Find practical help and resources to support you in using guidelines in your journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should adopt and implement reporting guidelines (and provide resources) to improve manuscript quality; use EQUATOR resources to operationalise guideline use in editorial and peer-review processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training and courses to improve writing and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Courses & events (e.g., Online Publication School) designed for early‑career researchers and students to improve the writing process and produce articles 'fit for purpose'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend EQUATOR training or Publication School to learn practical skills for writing, reporting, and navigating publication processes; training complements guideline use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on developing reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: How to develop a reporting guideline — resources and steps for guideline development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow EQUATOR guidance when developing new reporting guidelines to ensure methodological rigour, stakeholder involvement, and clear dissemination (useful for groups creating extensions or new topic-specific guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhance quality and transparency of health research
rubrics_metrics.description: Enhancing the QUAlity and Transparency Of health Research — overarching mission: find reporting guidelines, improve writing, join courses, run training, enhance peer review, implement guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim to improve research reporting by selecting appropriate guidelines, using toolkits and training, embedding guidelines in journal workflows, and applying them during peer review to increase transparency, reproducibility and usability of research.
